bug_report_content:
Title: [math] Complex Tanh for "big" numbers
Type: Bug | Priority: Minor | Status: Closed | Resolution: Fixed

Description:
Hi,

In Complex.java the tanh is computed with the following formula:

tanh(a + bi) = sinh(2a)/(cosh(2a)+cos(2b)) + [sin(2b)/(cosh(2a)+cos(2b))]i

The problem that I'm finding is that as soon as "a" is a "big" number,
both sinh(2a) and cosh(2a) are infinity and then the method tanh returns in
the real part NaN (infinity/infinity) when it should return 1.0.

Wouldn't it be appropiate to add something as in the FastMath library??:

if (real>20.0){
      return createComplex(1.0, 0.0);
}
if (real<-20.0){
      return createComplex(-1.0, 0.0);
}


Best regards,

JBB

Comments:

[Sebastien Brisard]: Even when a is not large enough to cause overflows, I'm not sure the general expression used is quite accurate (because {{cosh(2 * a)}} and {{sinh(2 * a)}} are very close, but not equal). I've often come accross this issue, and found that reverting to exponential representation (keeping only the exponentials with negative argument) was much better behaved.

In the present case, maybe the following representation of the real part
{{(1 - exp(-4 * a)) / (1 + 2 * exp(-2 * a) * cos(2 * b) + exp(-4 * a))}}
would avoid overflows (for {{a > 0}}, while remaining fairly accurate (otherwise, the threshold needs to be tuned).

Similar expressions can be derived for {{a < 0}}.

What do you think?
Sébastien

[Luc Maisonobe]: Very good idea Sébastien. Using stable formulas according to argument size is surely a good thing. We can also use FastMath.expm1() both in numerator and denominator, it will improve accuracy when a is close to 0.

[Sebastien Brisard]: I've run some tests comparing the two formulas: I didn't notice any major difference. Therefore I suggest to stick with the existing formula.
Meanwhile, the fix proposed by Juan must be implemented. It can be proved mathematically that for any value of {{b}}, the value of {{tanh(a + i * b)}} is within one ulp of 1.0 for {{abs(a) > 18.9}}, so the proposed threshold (20.0) is fairly safe, and consistent with other parts of CM. Note that the same fix must be implemented for {{tan}} also.

[Sebastien Brisard]: Changes proposed by Juan committed in {{r1236548}}.
